headline.title: Erling Haaland Is Everywhere at the World Cup. Most of It Is AI
headline.summary: Norwegian striker Erling Haaland has transcended his role as a footballer, becoming a prominent internet figure through fan engagement and AI-generated content. This phenomenon highlights the intersection of sports and technology, as AI plays a significant role in shaping his online presence.

articles.title: British Space Startup Launches Longevity Lab Into Orbit
articles.summary: A British space startup has successfully launched a longevity lab into orbit, which will transmit data to aid in the development of AI models focused on understanding the behavior of proteins associated with age-related diseases such as Alzheimer's and certain cancers. This initiative aims to enhance research and predictive capabilities in the field of longevity and health.

articles.title: LeRobot v0.6.0: Imagine, Evaluate, Improve
articles.summary: LeRobot v0.6.0 has been released, featuring enhanced capabilities for imagining, evaluating, and improving AI-generated content. The update includes new algorithms aimed at optimizing performance and user experience.

articles.title: Your family’s $300 stake in OpenAI
articles.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has reiterated his commitment to ensuring that Americans benefit from the wealth generated by AI, as reported by the Financial Times. The discussion centers around a potential initiative that could allow families to invest in OpenAI, with a suggested stake of $300.

articles.title: The first American autonomous ground vehicles are fighting in Ukraine
articles.summary: Forterra has deployed over 100 autonomous ground vehicles in Ukraine, marking the first use of American autonomous technology in combat. These vehicles are designed to support military operations by enhancing logistical capabilities on the battlefield.

articles.title: The ‘first’ AI-run ransomware attack still needed a human
articles.summary: The first known instance of an AI agent executing a ransomware attack revealed that human involvement was still crucial, as a person selected the victim, established the infrastructure, and provided stolen credentials. This indicates that while AI played a role in the technical execution, the attack was not entirely autonomous.

articles.title: Efficient bias mitigation in T2I diffusion models using Concept Graphs
articles.summary: Researchers have introduced CO-ALIGN, a new bias mitigation method for text-to-image diffusion models that utilizes concept-graph alignment to address harmful biases inherited from training data. This approach aims to improve the coherence of generated outputs by intervening more effectively than existing techniques that focus solely on the text encoder or inference-time guidance.

articles.title: Nemotron-Labs-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B: Compressing Hybrid MoE LLMs
articles.summary: Nemotron-Labs-3-Puzzle-75B-A9B is a compressed version of the Nemotron-3-Super model, optimized for interactive deployment to enhance server throughput. It reportedly achieves nearly double the server throughput compared to its predecessor under similar user throughput conditions.

articles.title: AgentGym2: Benchmarking Large Language Model Agents in De-Idealized Real-World Environments
articles.summary: The article introduces AgentGym2, a new benchmarking framework designed to evaluate large language model agents in more realistic and complex real-world environments. It highlights the limitations of existing benchmarks that often simplify conditions and fail to account for the challenges agents face in practical applications.

articles.title: GLM-5 Serving Parameter Tuning for OpenClaw: Single-Deployment MaaS Inference Optimization for Long-Context Agent Workloads
articles.summary: The article discusses the optimization of GLM-5 serving parameters for OpenClaw, focusing on enhancing inference performance for long-context agent workloads that involve extensive input and output tokens. It highlights the importance of throughput, time-to-first-token (TTFT), and tail latency in ensuring high-quality service in a multi-model inference environment.

articles.title: K9-Bench: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs on Canine-Centric Videos
articles.summary: The article introduces K9-Bench, a framework designed to evaluate multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on canine-centric videos. It emphasizes the importance of benchmarking AI models in understanding animal behavior and enhancing pet-related applications, such as recognizing distress signals and developing responsive robotic companions.

articles.title: Gemma 4 Technical Report
articles.summary: Gemma 4 is a new series of open-weight, multimodal language models that enhance compute efficiency and reasoning capabilities, featuring architectures with 2.3B to 31B parameters. The model suite includes advanced vision and audio encoders, as well as a unified, encoder-free architecture for the 12B model that processes raw audio.
